statement: Joint convergence near a strict interior optimizer confines every competing nuisance choice to every neighborhood of that optimizer.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {A E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] {l : Filter A} {D : Set E} (hD : IsOpen D) {f : A → E → ℝ} {g : E → ℝ} {p : E} {q : A → E} (hp : p ∈ D) (hjoint : ∀ y ∈ D, Tendsto (fun av : A × E ↦ f av.1 av.2) (l ×ˢ 𝓝 y) (𝓝 (g y))) (hstrict : ∀ y ∈ D, y ≠ p → g y < g p) (hconc : ∀ᶠ a in l, ConcaveOn ℝ D (f a)) (hq : ∀ᶠ a in l, q a ∈ D ∧ f a p ≤ f a (q a)) : Tendsto q l (𝓝 p)
dossier_scope_note: Generic lemma used by emg, ht and sn. This row supplies no independent family coverage.

statement: A strict joint derivative and convergence of the nuisance optimizer give the profile derivative by comparing two secants with fixed nuisance coordinates.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] {f : ℝ → E → ℝ} {P : ℝ → ℝ} {t : ℝ} {p : E} {q : ℝ → E} {D : (ℝ × E) →L[ℝ] ℝ} (hd : HasStrictFDerivAt (fun ap : ℝ × E ↦ f ap.1 ap.2) D (t,p)) (hq : Tendsto q (𝓝 t) (𝓝 p)) (hP : P t = f t p) (hmax : ∀ᶠ a in 𝓝 t, f a p ≤ P a ∧ P a = f a (q a) ∧ f t (q a) ≤ P t) : HasDerivAt P (D (1,0)) t
dossier_scope_note: Generic lemma used by emg, ht and sn. This row supplies no independent family coverage.

statement: As dimensionless shape tends to zero, the optimized likelihood converges to the exponential fit on the sample shifted by its minimum.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} {x : Fin n → ℝ} (hx : LocationScale.Nonconstant x) (i : Fin n) (hi : ∀ j, x i ≤ x j) : Tendsto (rateProfile x) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 (Exponential.logLik (fun j ↦ x j-x i) (Exponential.rate (fun j ↦ x j-x i))))

statement: As dimensionless shape tends to infinity, the optimized likelihood converges to the ordinary all-free normal fit.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} {x : Fin n → ℝ} (hx : LocationScale.Nonconstant x) : Tendsto (rateProfile x) atTop (𝓝 (Normal.logLik x (Normal.mean x) (Normal.sd x (Normal.mean x))))

statement: The assigned face values extend the actual profile continuously on the closed chart, and the interior profile is differentiable.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} {x : Fin n → ℝ} (hx : LocationScale.Nonconstant x) (i : Fin n) (hi : ∀ j, x i ≤ x j) : ContinuousOn (compactProfile x i) (Icc 0 1) ∧ DifferentiableOn ℝ (compactProfile x i) (Ioo 0 1) ∧ EqOn (compactProfile x i) (interiorProfile x) (Ioo 0 1)

statement: A nonconstant sample has a finite fit exactly when an interior stationary value reaches both optimized faces.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} {x : Fin n → ℝ} (hx : LocationScale.Nonconstant x) (i : Fin n) (hi : ∀ j, x i ≤ x j) : (∃ t ∈ Ioo 0 1, HasDerivAt (compactProfile x i) 0 t ∧ max (compactProfile x i 0) (compactProfile x i 1) ≤ compactProfile x i t) ↔ ∃ q ∈ (Ioo 0 1 ×ˢ LocationScale.domain), IsMaxOn (fun p : ℝ × (ℝ × ℝ) ↦ shapeLogLik x ((1-p.1)/p.1) p.2) (Ioo 0 1 ×ˢ LocationScale.domain) q
dossier_scope_note: Nonconstant branch. Read with constant_log_unbounded for constant samples.

statement: With a common observation, shrinking the scale at fixed dimensionless shape makes the log likelihood unbounded.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (m : ℝ) : ¬ BddAbove ((fun p : ℝ × (ℝ × ℝ) ↦ shapeLogLik (fun _ : Fin n ↦ m) ((1-p.1)/p.1) p.2) '' (Ioo 0 1 ×ˢ LocationScale.domain))

statement: If a nonconstant sample has no finite maximizer, the larger optimized face is its exact unattained supremum.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} {x : Fin n → ℝ} (hx : LocationScale.Nonconstant x) (i : Fin n) (hi : ∀ j, x i ≤ x j) (h : ¬ ∃ q ∈ (Ioo 0 1 ×ˢ LocationScale.domain), IsMaxOn (fun p : ℝ × (ℝ × ℝ) ↦ shapeLogLik x ((1-p.1)/p.1) p.2) (Ioo 0 1 ×ˢ LocationScale.domain) q) : IsLUB ((fun p : ℝ × (ℝ × ℝ) ↦ shapeLogLik x ((1-p.1)/p.1) p.2) '' (Ioo 0 1 ×ˢ LocationScale.domain)) (max (compactProfile x i 0) (compactProfile x i 1))
dossier_scope_note: Paired with all_free_criterion and constant_log_unbounded. Exact real-arithmetic failure classification.

statement: The all-free likelihood is unbounded exactly when a strict majority of observations equal the minimum.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} (x : Fin n → ℝ) {i : Fin n} (hi : ∀ j, x i ≤ x j) : (¬ BddAbove ((fun p : ℝ × (ℝ × ℝ) ↦ likelihood x p.1 p.2.1 p.2.2) '' domain x)) ↔ n < 2 * TDist.multiplicity x (x i)

statement: Finite attainment is equivalent to at most half minimum ties and an eligible floor or stationary shape that reaches both faces.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} (x : Fin n → ℝ) {i : Fin n} (hi : ∀ j, x i ≤ x j) : (∃ p ∈ domain x, IsMaxOn (fun p ↦ likelihood x p.1 p.2.1 p.2.2) (domain x) p) ↔ 2 * TDist.multiplicity x (x i) ≤ n ∧ ∃ ν ≥ (1 : ℝ), 0 < TDist.exponent x (x i) ν ∧ (ν = 1 ∨ HasDerivAt (scaleProfile x (x i)) 0 ν) ∧ max (normalFace x (x i)) (collapseFace x (x i)) ≤ scaleProfile x (x i) ν

statement: Below or at a half tie, failure of finite attainment leaves the larger of the half-normal and applicable scale-zero values as the exact supremum.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} (x : Fin n → ℝ) {i : Fin n} (hi : ∀ j, x i ≤ x j) (hc : 2 * TDist.multiplicity x (x i) ≤ n) (h : ¬ ∃ p ∈ domain x, IsMaxOn (fun p ↦ likelihood x p.1 p.2.1 p.2.2) (domain x) p) : IsLUB ((fun p : ℝ × (ℝ × ℝ) ↦ likelihood x p.1 p.2.1 p.2.2) '' domain x) (max (normalFace x (x i)) (collapseFace x (x i)))
dossier_scope_note: Paired with all_free_unbounded_iff for majority ties and all_free_criterion for finite equality.

statement: The objective in the inverse-scale chart is exactly the physical skew-normal log likelihood.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} (x : Fin n → ℝ) (α : ℝ) (p : LocationScale.domain) : objective x α (LocationScale.inverseEquiv p) = logLik α x p

statement: A compact nuisance set contains every parameter choice in a fixed log-likelihood superlevel, uniformly over slant.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} {x : Fin n → ℝ} (hx : LocationScale.Nonconstant x) (L : ℝ) : ∃ K : Set LocationScale.inverseDomain, IsCompact K ∧ ∀ (α : ℝ) (p : LocationScale.inverseDomain), L ≤ objective x α p → p ∈ K

statement: The entire sufficiently positive slant tail lies strictly below the optimized right half-normal face.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} {x : Fin n → ℝ} (hx : LocationScale.Nonconstant x) (i : Fin n) (hi : ∀ j, x i ≤ x j) : ∃ A > 0, ∀ α ≥ A, ∀ p ∈ LocationScale.inverseDomain, objective x α p < face x (x i)

statement: The entire sufficiently negative slant tail lies strictly below the optimized left half-normal face.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} {x : Fin n → ℝ} (hx : LocationScale.Nonconstant x) (i : Fin n) (hi : ∀ j, x j ≤ x i) : ∃ A > 0, ∀ α ≤ -A, ∀ p ∈ LocationScale.inverseDomain, objective x α p < face x (x i)

statement: The optimized right face is reached along a moving-location path, with full weight at tied minima.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} {x : Fin n → ℝ} (hx : LocationScale.Nonconstant x) (i : Fin n) (hi : ∀ j, x i ≤ x j) : Tendsto (fun t : ℝ ↦ logLik (t^2) x (x i-t⁻¹,Normal.sd x (x i))) atTop (𝓝 (face x (x i)))

statement: The optimized left face is reached along a moving-location path, with full weight at tied maxima.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} {x : Fin n → ℝ} (hx : LocationScale.Nonconstant x) (i : Fin n) (hi : ∀ j, x j ≤ x i) : Tendsto (fun t : ℝ ↦ logLik (-(t^2)) x (x i+t⁻¹,Normal.sd x (x i))) atTop (𝓝 (face x (x i)))

statement: A nonconstant sample attains a finite maximum exactly when a finite point reaches the larger optimized half-normal likelihood.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} {x : Fin n → ℝ} (hx : LocationScale.Nonconstant x) (i j : Fin n) (hi : ∀ k, x i ≤ x k) (hj : ∀ k, x k ≤ x j) : (∃ p : ℝ × LocationScale.inverseDomain, IsMaxOn (fun ap : ℝ × LocationScale.inverseDomain ↦ objective x ap.1 ap.2) univ p) ↔ ∃ (α : ℝ) (p : LocationScale.inverseDomain), max (face x (x i)) (face x (x j)) ≤ objective x α p
dossier_scope_note: Read with constant_unbounded for constant data.

statement: If a nonconstant sample has no finite fit, the larger optimized half-normal value is its supremum.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} {x : Fin n → ℝ} (hx : LocationScale.Nonconstant x) (i j : Fin n) (hi : ∀ k, x i ≤ x k) (hj : ∀ k, x k ≤ x j) (h : ¬ ∃ p : ℝ × LocationScale.inverseDomain, IsMaxOn (fun ap : ℝ × LocationScale.inverseDomain ↦ objective x ap.1 ap.2) univ p) : IsLUB (range (fun ap : ℝ × LocationScale.inverseDomain ↦ objective x ap.1 ap.2)) (max (face x (x i)) (face x (x j)))
dossier_scope_note: Read with all_free_criterion and constant_unbounded. This does not certify a numerical detector.

statement: The finite witness can equivalently be required to lie at a stationary slant of the nuisance profile.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} {x : Fin n → ℝ} (hx : LocationScale.Nonconstant x) (i j : Fin n) (hi : ∀ k, x i ≤ x k) (hj : ∀ k, x k ≤ x j) : (∃ p : ℝ × LocationScale.inverseDomain, IsMaxOn (fun ap : ℝ × LocationScale.inverseDomain ↦ objective x ap.1 ap.2) univ p) ↔ ∃ α : ℝ, HasDerivAt (profile x) 0 α ∧ max (face x (x i)) (face x (x j)) ≤ profile x α

statement: The profiled likelihood has the right and left optimized half-normal limits at positive and negative infinite slant.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} {x : Fin n → ℝ} (hx : LocationScale.Nonconstant x) (i j : Fin n) (hi : ∀ k, x i ≤ x k) (hj : ∀ k, x k ≤ x j) : Tendsto (profile x) atTop (𝓝 (face x (x i))) ∧ Tendsto (profile x) atBot (𝓝 (face x (x j)))

statement: A nonempty constant sample gives unbounded all-free likelihood.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (m : ℝ) : ¬ BddAbove (range (fun ap : ℝ × LocationScale.inverseDomain ↦ objective (fun _ : Fin n ↦ m) ap.1 ap.2))

statement: With positive size and beta held and at least one positive count, the alpha score crosses zero exactly once, from positive to negative. The root is the unique maximum.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) {x : Fin n → ℕ} (hx : ∃ i, 0 < x i) {r b : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) (hb : 0 < b) : let f := fun t ↦ averageLogMass x r t b ∃ a > 0, HasDerivAt f 0 a ∧ (∀ t ∈ Ioo 0 a, 0 < deriv f t) ∧ (∀ t > a, deriv f t < 0) ∧ (∀ t > 0, IsMaxOn f (Ioi 0) t ↔ t = a)

statement: With positive alpha and beta held and at least one positive count, the size score crosses zero exactly once, from positive to negative. The root is the unique maximum.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) {x : Fin n → ℕ} (hx : ∃ i, 0 < x i) {a b : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b) : let f := fun t ↦ averageLogMass x t a b ∃ r > 0, HasDerivAt f 0 r ∧ (∀ t ∈ Ioo 0 r, 0 < deriv f t) ∧ (∀ t > r, deriv f t < 0) ∧ (∀ t > 0, IsMaxOn f (Ioi 0) t ↔ t = r)

statement: With positive size and alpha held and at least one positive count, symmetry gives the same unique score root and maximum for beta.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) {x : Fin n → ℕ} (hx : ∃ i, 0 < x i) {r a : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) (ha : 0 < a) : let f := fun t ↦ averageLogMass x r a t ∃ b > 0, HasDerivAt f 0 b ∧ (∀ t ∈ Ioo 0 b, 0 < deriv f t) ∧ (∀ t > b, deriv f t < 0) ∧ (∀ t > 0, IsMaxOn f (Ioi 0) t ↔ t = b)

statement: Increasing dispersion and subtracting the log-binomial increment from the log-odds direction exposes the chosen adjacent pair. Along the ray the conditional product is the strict supremum.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {N n : ℕ} (hN : 2 ≤ N) (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → Fin (N + 1)) {l u : Fin (N + 1)} (hlu : u.val = l.val + 1) (hx : ∀ i, x i = l ∨ x i = u) (η ν : ℝ) : let F : Finset (Fin (N + 1)) := {l,u} let a := edgeSlope N l.val (∀ k ∈ F, Tendsto (fun t ↦ mass N (η-t*a) (ν+t) k) atTop (𝓝 (conditionalMass η ν F k))) ∧ let U := ∏ i, conditionalMass η ν F (x i) IsLUB (range (fun t ↦ likelihood x (η-t*a) (ν+t))) U ∧ ∀ t, likelihood x (η-t*a) (ν+t) < U

statement: The midpoint of two adjacent directions isolates an interior cell. Its mass and the ray supremum for a constant sample are one.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {N n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → Fin (N + 1)) {k : Fin (N + 1)} (hk₀ : 0 < k.val) (hkN : k.val < N) (hx : ∀ i, x i = k) (η ν : ℝ) : let a := pointSlope N k.val Tendsto (fun t ↦ mass N (η+t*a) (ν+t) k) atTop (𝓝 1) ∧ IsLUB (range (fun t ↦ likelihood x (η+t*a) (ν+t))) 1 ∧ ∀ t, likelihood x (η+t*a) (ν+t) < 1

statement: Decreasing dispersion at fixed log odds isolates both endpoints. The strict ray supremum is the base likelihood conditioned on the two endpoints.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {N n : ℕ} (hN : 2 ≤ N) (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → Fin (N + 1)) (hx : ∀ i, x i = 0 ∨ x i = Fin.last N) (η ν : ℝ) : let F : Finset (Fin (N + 1)) := {0,Fin.last N} (∀ k ∈ F, Tendsto (fun t ↦ mass N η (ν-t) k) atTop (𝓝 (conditionalMass η ν F k))) ∧ let U := ∏ i, conditionalMass η ν F (x i) IsLUB (range (fun t ↦ likelihood x η (ν-t))) U ∧ ∀ t, likelihood x η (ν-t) < U

statement: At size at least two the finite canonical fit is unique exactly when the empirical moment vector is inside the moment hull.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {N n : ℕ} (hN : 2 ≤ N) (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → Fin (N + 1)) : (∃! θ : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2), IsMaxOn (fun θ ↦ likelihood x (θ 0) (θ 1)) univ θ) ↔ empirical x ∈ interior (convexHull ℝ (range (statistic N)))

statement: At size at least two, allowing probability endpoints adds precisely the two endpoint-constant cases to the interior-hull attainment criterion.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {N n : ℕ} (hN : 2 ≤ N) (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → Fin (N + 1)) : (∃ p ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1 ×ˢ (univ : Set ℝ), IsMaxOn (fun p : ℝ × ℝ ↦ closedLikelihood x p.1 p.2) (Icc 0 1 ×ˢ univ) p) ↔ (∀ i, x i = 0) ∨ (∀ i, x i = Fin.last N) ∨ empirical x ∈ interior (convexHull ℝ (range (statistic N)))
dossier_scope_note: At N≥2. Read with Discrete3CMB.size_zero_likelihood and Discrete3CMB.bernoulli_fit for sizes zero and one.

statement: Changing the log rate ratio while holding the product fixed multiplies the sample likelihood by an explicit exponential factor.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} (x : Fin n → ℤ) (a b u : ℝ) : likelihood x (a*exp u,b*exp (-u)) = exp ((n : ℝ)*(a+b-a*exp u-b*exp (-u)) + (∑ i, (x i : ℝ))*u) * likelihood x (a,b)

statement: At every joint maximum the rate difference equals the signed sample mean. The argument also covers feasible axes.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℤ) (p : ℝ × ℝ) (hp : p ∈ domain) (hm : IsMaxOn (likelihood x) domain p) : p.1-p.2 = (∑ i, (x i : ℝ))/n

statement: A balanced two-sign sample has a positive diagonal maximizer and every maximizer lies on the diagonal, for any magnitude histogram.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℤ) (hmean : ∑ i, x i = 0) (hpos : ∃ i, 0 < x i) (hneg : ∃ i, x i < 0) : (∃ r > 0, IsMaxOn (likelihood x) domain (r,r)) ∧ ∀ p ∈ domain, IsMaxOn (likelihood x) domain p → 0 < p.1 ∧ p.1 = p.2

statement: Swapping rates cannot produce a distinct maximizer of the same signed sample.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℤ) (p : ℝ × ℝ) (hp : p ∈ domain) (hm : IsMaxOn (likelihood x) domain p) (hs : IsMaxOn (likelihood x) domain (p.2, p.1)) : (p.2, p.1) = p

statement: On any mean-zero sample, exchanging positive rates preserves the likelihood.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} (x : Fin n → ℤ) (hmean : ∑ i, x i = 0) {a b : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b) : likelihood x (b,a) = likelihood x (a,b)

statement: Any positive rate pair matching the signed mean strictly beats every nonzero log-ratio tilt on its fixed-product slice.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℤ) {a b : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b) (hmean : a - b = (∑ i, (x i : ℝ)) / n) (u : ℝ) (hu : u ≠ 0) : likelihood x (a*exp u,b*exp (-u)) < likelihood x (a,b)

statement: Maximizing on the closed mean-matching set yields exactly the same maximizing set as the closed quadrant.
hypotheses_and_conclusion: {n : ℕ} (hn : 0 < n) (x : Fin n → ℤ) (p : ℝ × ℝ) : let C := {q ∈ domain | q.1-q.2 = (∑ i, (x i : ℝ))/n} (p ∈ domain ∧ IsMaxOn (likelihood x) domain p) ↔ p ∈ C ∧ IsMaxOn (likelihood x) C p
